rubric.finalThreshold: 99 accuracy /99 completeness and no unresolved material source issue after final scoped evidence
criteria: Public guest and admin token/challenge namespace isolation
Verified fixed GitHub owner, state/PKCE/replay/expiry controls
No public secured-content/admin access or provider login
Admin-only installability and cache privacy with legacy worker retirement
Truthful failure feedback, role-management semantics and release-scope documentation

findings.title: Nested manifest.ts is not a Next.js metadata route
findings.problem: The installed Next.js metadata matcher recognizes /manifest.ts but not /admin/manifest.ts. Moving the special file under admin does not create the required served manifest/link, so the retained admin PWA lacks its installability manifest.
findings.independentEvidence: Executed isMetadataRouteFile from next/dist/lib/metadata/is-metadata-route with page extensions js/jsx/ts/tsx: /manifest.ts returned true; /admin/manifest.ts returned false. Installed documentation explicitly locates this special convention at the app root.
findings.requiredChange: Use an explicit admin manifest route, such as app/admin/manifest.webmanifest/route.ts with application/manifest+json, and set metadata.manifest only in the admin layout. Keep root/public metadata without a manifest.
findings.validation: Production HTML for admin has the exact manifest link; endpoint200 returns correct id/start_url/scope/icons; public / and /play have no manifest or install UI; actual admin worker/controller/offline checks pass.

findings.title: Display the controlled OAuth failure state
findings.problem: Callback errors redirect to /admin?auth=failed, but the admin page does not read that parameter and no UI handles it. A denied account, invalid state, expired challenge or provider failure returns to an indistinguishable sign-in screen without explaining rejection/recovery.
findings.requiredChange: Render a controlled admin-only failure message and retry link/button for this flag. Do not echo provider error descriptions, codes, tokens or arbitrary query text.
findings.validation: Wrong-account and callback-error fixture paths show safe feedback and no admin content; refresh/retry remains usable.

designFollowups.detail: Existing Users and access text says granted moderators/admins gain site capabilities. Under the new fixed-owner gate they cannot authenticate to admin even if database roles are granted. Remove/disable obsolete delegation controls or clearly label retained roles as historical/inactive under this release. Do not imply granting a role permits a second GitHub user. This is a scope/UX inconsistency, not an identified server bypass.

Root retirement/unregistration and namespaced cache deletion are appropriate. Test an already-controlled root client plus an existing admin registration. Do not claim that code can remove an already-installed OS icon or prevent generic browser bookmark creation. Explain any required reload/uninstall separately.

Verify that standalone admin navigation can leave for GitHub and return with the admin cookie in the intended browser/PWA context. Browser fixture routing cannot certify physical iOS installation or cookie-context continuity.

positiveArchitectureAssessment: Separate admin digest domain and wp_admin/wp_admin_login cookies preserve guest/admin token isolation; a raw token copied between cookies hashes differently. Public member sessions are denied and public actors forced to player.
Fixed numeric GitHub ID plus login check is stronger than trusting login hint or profile name. Both must match the verified /user response before member-session creation.

S256 PKCE, random state, single-use expiring challenge, fixed provider URLs, redirect:error and server-side client secret/token handling align with official GitHub App web authentication. No provider access/refresh token persistence was found.

Admin content/users routes derive their actor from adminSession and pass only that verified ID into trusted repository configuration. Public role claims and old configured-admin allowlists do not open these routes.

Admin worker caches only generic offline/icons, intercepts admin GET navigations only, and does not cache API/RSC/private pages or queue mutations. Legacy cleanup targets only prior Wordpairs root worker/cache names.
finalEvidenceRequired: Unit/transport wrong ID with correct login, wrong login with correct ID, bad state/PKCE, replay, expired challenge, provider failure and unsupported redirect tests.

Actual composition tests copy guest token into admin cookie and admin token into guest cookie; both fail. Old member/public and role-bearing guest sessions remain player-only or denied as appropriate.

Admin callback success sets only admin cookies, preserves existing guest session/room identity, and logout revokes the admin DB session without signing out the guest. No admin guest-creation endpoint exists.
Admin API/direct-page denial for guests and non-owner GitHub identity, including client-supplied profile/role fields.
Manifest/worker production checks including retirement of old public registration, no public install UI/manifest, no private CacheStorage entries, admin offline fallback and API network failure.

Record actual GitHub App permissions, callbacks and owner restriction after creation; no provider-success claim before a real authorized flow. Preserve historical approvals/tests as superseded evidence rather than silently changing their claimed scope.

disposition: Repair the manifest route and controlled callback-error feedback; reconcile obsolete ACL UI semantics. Identity separation is a sound direction with no concrete bypass found in this read-only pass, but final approval requires the listed boundary and production-PWA evidence.
